checks.name: Failure atomicity, rejected-operation side effects, restart/recovery, concurrency
checks.method: read decode_activation_plan/result_from_error/build_model/BytesResult; ran the full negative suite and confirmed each case leaves `plan` disengaged; inspected the value type for synchronization/global state
checks.result: pass: every non-accepted result is constructed by result_from_error (lines 90-95), which never engages DecodeResult.plan; the fixed pipeline order (limits -> parse -> shape -> version -> digest -> capability/reference/status -> entity caps -> accepted) means the first failing step determines code/target and no later step runs. build_model writes to a local ActivationPlan and is moved into the result only on success (lines 1469-1477), so a failed decode cannot leak a partial or mutated value. The unit retains no state between calls, so restart/recovery and rejected-operation persistence are not applicable, and ActivationPlan is a plain aggregate with no lock, no virtual function, and no aliasing of the input buffer (shareable read-only).
